text: dittoViz functions: use dittoViz_<PlotName> (e.g., dittoViz_scatterPlot dittoViz::scatterPlot) plotthis functions: use plotthis_<PlotName> (e.g., plotthis_AreaPlot plotthis::AreaPlot) custom/standalone functions: use plot name directly (e.g., linePlot, piePlot) adding brand-new plotting function (e.g., piePlot), define document plot function first, wrap module. Create three core files: R/<moduleName>_module_ui.R, R/<moduleName>_module_server.R, R/<moduleName>_module_app.R. Document UI, server, app functions roxygen (@export, params, examples). @section Plot parameters implemented altered functionality: - List inputs exposed @section Plot parameters defaults: - Document exposed parameters UI labels defaults @section Plot parameters implementing new functionality: - Document new plotly-specific controls (axes, ticks, reference lines, etc) Add example app uses module twice prove multi-instance behavior. Wire reactive defaults support parent apps can drive parameters app state (see Supporting Reactive Defaults). Freeze input update server plot render twice (see Updating Inputs Server). Wire manual layout-edit persistence user-dragged titles, legends, annotations, colorbars survive re-renders (see Persisting Manual Layout Edits). Cover base plotting function testthat; cover module/app testServer feasible. Note ggplotly conversion quirks change drop functionality. Never use eval(str2expression()) raw user input. Use safe_eval_filter(), validate_expression(), safe_resolve_adj_fxn() instead (see Sanitizing User-Provided Expressions ).

code: library(VizModules) library(drc)  register_model_backend("drm", list(     fit = function(formula, data, drc_fct = "LL.4", ...) {         fct_map <- list(             "LL.4" = drc::LL.4, "LL.3" = drc::LL.3, "LL.2" = drc::LL.2,             "W1.4" = drc::W1.4, "W2.4" = drc::W2.4         )         fct_fn <- fct_map[[drc_fct]]         if (is.null(fct_fn)) stop("Unknown drc family: ", drc_fct)         drc::drm(formula, data = data, fct = fct_fn())     },     predict = function(model, newdata) {         as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = newdata))     },     validate_classes = "drc",     fields = list(         drc_fct = list(             type = "select",             args = list(choices = c("LL.4", "LL.3", "LL.2", "W1.4", "W2.4"),                         selected = "LL.4")         )     ) ))  # Launch — "drm" now appears in the dropdown with a "Drc fct" selector data(ryegrass, package = "drc") dittoViz_scatterPlotApp(data_list = list("ryegrass" = ryegrass))

code: library(VizModules)  minimalModuleUI <- function(id) {     ns <- NS(id)     tagList(         h4("Minimal Module Controls"),         # Custom input - uses the module's namespace         checkboxInput(ns("filter_setosa"), "Start with Setosa Only", value = FALSE),         hr(),         # Base module UI - pass the bare 'id', not ns(id)         dittoViz_scatterPlotInputsUI(id, iris)     ) }  minimalModuleOutput <- function(id) {     # Simply delegate to the base module's output UI     dittoViz_scatterPlotOutputUI(id) }

title: Building Custom Modules
text: pattern? moduleServer(id, ...) gives us access input$filter_setosa, namespaced wrapper’s id. calling dittoViz_scatterPlotServer(id, filtered_data) outside moduleServer() closure, base module attaches namespace UI, nested one. called dittoViz_scatterPlotServer() inside moduleServer() block, create nested namespaces like id-id-x_axis, wouldn’t match actual input IDs UI.
code: minimalModuleServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {     # Step 1: Process data inside a moduleServer block     # This gives us access to inputs namespaced to 'id' (our module's inputs)     filtered_data <- moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {         reactive({             req(data_reactive())             df <- data_reactive()              # Input specific to this custom module             if (isTRUE(input$filter_setosa)) {                 if ("Species" %in% names(df)) {                     df <- df[df$Species == "setosa", ]                 }             }             df         })     })      # Step 2: Call the base module server OUTSIDE the moduleServer block     # This is critical! If we called this inside the moduleServer above,     # dittoViz_scatterPlotServer would look for inputs at id-id-inputName instead of id-inputName     dittoViz_scatterPlotServer(id, filtered_data) }

title: Filtering Data with the dataFilter Module
text: dataFilter module renders interactive table filter box every column returns rows user left visible. hands filtered data back reactive, can plug front plotting module plot always reflects current table filters. Like every module VizModules, comes two halves share id: dataFilterUI(id) – places table UI. dataFilterServer(id, data, ...) – runs table returns filtered data.

title: Filtering Data with the dataFilter Module
text: server small, job easy describe: Prepare data. default (factor.char.cols = TRUE) every character column converted factor. purely cosmetic: makes DT show drop-select filter columns instead free-text search box. Render table. DT table drawn filter row top column (filter = "top"). Return visible rows. DT continuously reports rows survive current filters via input$table_rows_all. module subsets data rows, calls droplevels() filtered-categories don’t linger plot legends axes, returns result reactive. Conceptually:
code: data (reactive) --> character cols to factors --> DT table (user filters)                                                         |                                      input$table_rows_all (visible rows)                                                         v                                               filtered data (reactive)

what: Reactive defaults: driving inputs from app state
title: Defaults and Hiding Controls
text: Sometimes parameter needs follow app rather fixed . common case colour mapping track column user selected elsewhere app. , individual entry defaults may reactive() reactiveVal() instead plain value: Pass list *InputsUI() *Server(), static defaults. UI needs access reactive, build inside renderUI() (UI seed taken isolate(), cause controls re-render whenever reactive changes). get three guarantees: parameter tracks reactive. Every change flows plot. control stays correct editable. Color selector shows current column, user can still change . plot renders per change. value resolved server-side, reactive flush data, flicker. Semantics worth knowing: external change always wins. user picked different colour column module changes app-level selector, selector’s value replaces choice. Reset restores reactive’s current value, value held startup. reactive() reactiveVal() recognised. plain function treated literal default value, something call. Composite widgets sync cosmetically . plot always uses current value, compound control accept generic value message — custom.models scatter module one watch — re-display . Reactive defaults supported input.

what: Hiding inputs dynamically in a custom module
title: Defaults and Hiding Controls
text: building wrapper module (see vignette("custom-modules", package = "VizModules")), can hide show inputs runtime response inputs using shinyjs: Note shinyjs::hide() / shinyjs::show() act input element . reflow behaviour (empty gap), use hide_input() / show_input() helpers instead, target wrapping cell flexbox grid:
code: library(shinyjs)  myModuleServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {     moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {         # Hide the 'size' input whenever a size.by column is chosen         observe({             if (nzchar(input$size.by)) {                 shinyjs::hide(id = "size")             } else {                 shinyjs::show(id = "size")             }         })     })      dittoViz_scatterPlotServer(id, data_reactive) } myModuleServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {     moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {         observe({             if (nzchar(input$size.by)) {                 VizModules::hide_input(session, "size")             } else {                 VizModules::show_input(session, "size")             }         })     })      dittoViz_scatterPlotServer(id, data_reactive) }

text: provide collect_source_data() assemble compact record plotted data, stats, UI inputs, rendered plot, create_source_download_handler() turn record downloadable .zip. collect_source_data() requires reactive plotly plot; output summary can optionally enriched stats reactive UI inputs reactive. create_source_download_handler() also accepts named list summaries (one per plot), Panel Builder bundles every plot canvas single download.
code: if (interactive()) {     library(shiny)     library(plotly)      ui <- fluidPage(         plotlyOutput("plot"),         downloadButton("download_summary", "Download Summary")     )      server <- function(input, output, session) {         # A reactive plotly plot         plot_reactive <- reactive({             plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers")         })          # Optional: a reactive returning a stats data.frame         stats_reactive <- reactive({             data.frame(                 metric = c("mean_mpg", "sd_mpg"),                 value  = c(mean(mtcars$mpg), sd(mtcars$mpg))             )         })          # Optional: capture all UI inputs as a named list         AllInputs <- reactive({             reactiveValuesToList(input)         })          output$plot <- renderPlotly(plot_reactive())          # Assemble the summary, then wire up the download handler.         plot_summary_reactive <- reactive({             collect_source_data(                 plot_reactive   = plot_reactive,                 stats_reactive  = stats_reactive,                 inputs_reactive = AllInputs()             )         })          output$download_summary <- create_source_download_handler(             data_list     = plot_summary_reactive,             filename_base = "my_plot_summary"         )     }      shinyApp(ui, server) }

what: Using the stat helpers in a custom module
title: Statistical Testing
text: pipeline fully exported: compute_pairwise_stats() — run tests, return data frame. create_stat_annotations() — convert results plotly shapes annotations. apply_stat_annotations() — append plotly figure. Axis coordinates. create_stat_annotations() positions brackets using 1-based categorical x-coordinates, matching figures built ggplotly() (every VizModules plot module ). build figure raw plot_ly(type = "box") call instead, plotly uses 0-based category positions brackets appear shifted one category right — prefer ggplotly() ggplot object stay consistent modules.
code: library(VizModules) library(ggplot2) library(plotly)  stats_df <- compute_pairwise_stats(     df   = example_iris,     x    = "Species",     y    = "Sepal.Length",     test = "wilcox.test",     p.adjust.method = "holm" )  # Build the figure with ggplot2 + ggplotly(), matching how the plot modules # construct their figures. This matters for bracket placement: ggplotly() # categorical axes are 1-based (the first factor level sits at x = 1), which # is the convention create_stat_annotations() expects. p <- ggplot(example_iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length)) +     geom_boxplot() fig <- ggplotly(p)  stat_result <- create_stat_annotations(     stats_df = stats_df,     fig      = fig,     df       = example_iris,     x        = "Species",     y        = "Sepal.Length",     display  = "symbol" )  apply_stat_annotations(fig, stat_result)

title: Input UI components for the ComplexHeatmap module — ComplexHeatmap_HeatmapInputsUI
text: following ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap() parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: matrix.cols - Numeric columns forming matrix (UI: "Matrix Columns", default: numeric columns) rowname.col - Column used row names (UI: "Row Name Column", default: "") name - Heatmap / legend title (UI: "Heatmap Name", default: "value") na_col - Color NA cells (UI: "NA Color", default: "grey") scale - Z-score matrix row, column, (UI: "Scale", default: "None"). Applied plotting — row/column annotation values source-data download always use unscaled matrix. reverse.palette - Reverse palette (UI: "Reverse Palette", default: FALSE) low_color, mid_color, high_color - Colors low/mid/high end value scale, .e. col ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap() built via circlize::colorRamp2() (UI: "Low/Mid/High Color", default: blue/white/red) min_value, mid_value, max_value - Values mapped low_color/mid_color/high_color (UI: "Min/Mid/Max Value", default: NA = derived matrix: min, mean(range(mat)), max respectively) show_heatmap_legend - Show heatmap legend (UI: "Show Legend", default: TRUE) border - Draw heatmap border (UI: "Border", default: FALSE) cluster_rows - Cluster rows (UI: "Cluster Rows", default: TRUE) cluster_columns - Cluster columns (UI: "Cluster Columns", default: TRUE) clustering_distance_rows - Row distance metric (UI: "Row Distance", default: "euclidean") clustering_distance_columns - Column distance metric (UI: "Column Distance", default: "euclidean") clustering_method_rows - Row linkage method (UI: "Row Method", default: "complete") clustering_method_columns - Column linkage method (UI: "Column Method", default: "complete") show_row_dend - Show row dendrogram (UI: "Show Row Dendrogram", default: TRUE) show_column_dend - Show column dendrogram (UI: "Show Column Dendrogram", default: TRUE) row_split_by - Row split method: "None", "K-means", "Hierarchical" (UI: "Row Split Method", default: "None"). one split mechanism ever active per axis, avoids error ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap() raises k-means hierarchical split requested . row_split_n - Number row groups, used row_split_by "None" (UI: "Row Groups", default: NA; clamped number matrix rows) column_split_by - Column split method: "None", "K-means", "Hierarchical" (UI: "Column Split Method", default: "None") column_split_n - Number column groups, used column_split_by "None" (UI: "Column Groups", default: NA; clamped number matrix columns) row_gap - Gap row slices, mm (UI: "Row Gap (mm)", default: 1) column_gap - Gap column slices, mm (UI: "Column Gap (mm)", default: 1) row_title - Row title (UI: "Row Title", default: "") column_title - Column title (UI: "Column Title", default: "") show_row_names - Show row names (UI: "Show Row Names", default: TRUE) show_column_names - Show column names (UI: "Show Column Names", default: TRUE) row_names_side - Row names side (UI: "Row Names Side", default: "right") column_names_side - Column names side (UI: "Column Names Side", default: "bottom") column_names_rot - Column name rotation (UI: "Column Name Rotation", default: 90) row_names_fontsize - Row name font size (UI: "Row Name Size", default: 12) column_names_fontsize - Column name font size (UI: "Column Name Size", default: 12) title_fontsize - Row/column title font size (UI: "Title Size", default: 13.2) row_annotations - Row annotation tracks, built ComplexHeatmap::rowAnnotation() passed left_annotation/right_annotation per row (UI: "Annotations" tab, "Row Annotations" multiDynamicInput() — row picks matrix column side, Left Right; default: none). row's color control appears just list column picked: numeric columns get Low/Mid/High color pickers, everything else gets multiColorPicker() one color per level. column_key - Column column_annotations matched matrix's selected column names (UI: "Annotations" tab, "Column Key"; shown data supplies column_annotations table) column_annotations - Column annotation tracks, built ComplexHeatmap::columnAnnotation() passed top_annotation/bottom_annotation per row (UI: "Annotations" tab, "Column Annotations" multiDynamicInput() — row picks column side, Top Bottom, per-row color controls row annotations; shown data supplies column_annotations table; default: none)

One "wilcox.test", "t.test", "kruskal.test", "anova". p.adjust.method Character; method p-value adjustment via stats::p.adjust(). Default "holm". paired Logical; whether perform paired tests ("wilcox.test" "t.test"). Default TRUE. sig.threshold Numeric; significance threshold * vs ns. P-values labeled *; labeled ns. Default 0.05. See sig.levels multi-star thresholds. sig.levels Named numeric vector; upper p-value bounds multi-star significance symbols. Names displayed symbols values thresholds. Default c("****" = 0.0001, "***" = 0.001, "**" = 0.01). number levels can provided. Evaluated smallest largest threshold significant symbol always wins.

title: Create plotly shapes and annotations for statistical test results — create_stat_annotations
text: stats_df Data frame compute_pairwise_stats(). fig plotly figure object. Used detect subplot axis pairs faceted plots. df original data frame. x Character; x-axis column name. y Character; y-axis column name. display Character; display: "p.adj", "p.value", "symbol". Default "p.adj". hide.ns Logical; hide non-significant results. Default FALSE. sig.threshold Numeric; significance threshold determining non-significant results. Default 0.05. line.color Character; color bracket lines. Default "#000000". line.width Numeric; width bracket lines. Default 1. bracket.style Character; "capped" ggpubr-style brackets vertical ticks, "flat" single horizontal line. Default "capped". group.Character NULL; nested grouping column. facet.Character NULL; faceting column. x.order Character vector; order x-axis categories. NULL, derived unique values x column. font.size Numeric; size annotation text. Default 12. step.increase Numeric; fraction y-range spacing successive brackets. Default 0.06. text.bump Numeric; fraction y-range vertical distance text bracket line. Default 0.04. bracket.inset Numeric; fixed amount inset bracket endpoint group center position. Creates visual separation adjacent brackets y-level. Default 0.025.

text: id ID Shiny module. Must match id used dataFilterUI(). data reactive containing data frame display filter. Values data frames coerced .data.frame(); NULL value treated "ready yet" table waits data. factor.char.cols Logical. TRUE, character columns data converted factors table rendered. causes DT display select-box filters columns instead free-text search boxes. Note DT serialises every level factor column page, best avoided columns many distinct values. Defaults TRUE. page.length Integer. default number rows shown per page. Defaults 10. col.visibility Logical. TRUE, adds DT "Columns" button (Buttons extension colvis) users can show/hide individual columns. Defaults FALSE. hide.columns Character vector column names (numeric vector column positions) hide table first drawn. Hidden columns get filter box, keeps interface focused columns matter. still present returned data, plotting modules can use . Set col.visibility = TRUE users able bring back; otherwise stay hidden. Names occur data ignored warning. Defaults NULL (show every column). filter.max.options Integer. maximum number options factor column's filter dropdown renders . Typing box narrows list, low cap keeps high-cardinality columns usable. Defaults 50.

title: Server logic for the dataFilter module — dataFilterServer
code: library(shiny) library(VizModules)  ui <- fluidPage(     dataFilterUI("filter"),     verbatimTextOutput("rows") )  server <- function(input, output, session) {     data <- reactive(iris)     # Petal columns are hidden on load, but the "Columns" button lets users     # bring them back, and they remain in the returned data either way.     filtered <- dataFilterServer("filter", data,         factor.char.cols = TRUE,         hide.columns = c("Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),         col.visibility = TRUE     )     output$rows <- renderPrint(nrow(filtered())) }  if (interactive()) shinyApp(ui, server)

what: Plot parameters not implemented or with altered functionality
title: Input UI components for the scatterPlot module — dittoViz_scatterPlotInputsUI
text: following dittoViz::scatterPlot() parameters available via UI inputs superseded: xlab - X-axis label (auto-generated reflect applied X adjustment, e.g. "log2(z-score(units))"; plotly allows interactive editing) ylab - Y-axis label (auto-generated reflect applied Y adjustment, e.g. "log2(z-score(units))"; plotly allows interactive editing) main - Plot title (plotly allows interactive editing) sub - Plot subtitle (supported plotly) theme - ggplot2 theme (applicable plotly) legend.title - Legend title (managed plotly interactively) legend.color.size - Legend color size (supported plotly) legend.shape.size - Legend shape size (supported plotly) add.xline - Use vline.intercepts instead vertical lines full styling options add.yline - Use hline.intercepts instead horizontal lines full styling options xline.linetype - Use vline.linetypes instead xline.color - Use vline.colors instead yline.linetype - Use hline.linetypes instead yline.color - Use hline.colors instead .letter - Lettering subplots (implemented plotly) .label - Labeling points interactively (compatible plotly hover) labels.size, labels.highlight, labels.use.numbers, labels.numbers.spacer, labels.repel, labels.repel.adjust, labels.split.- Point-label styling (tied .label, implemented) rename.color.groups - Rename color groups (implemented) rename.shape.groups - Rename shape groups (implemented) add.trajectory.curves - Add trajectory curves coordinate matrices (implemented; use add.trajectory..groups instead) .raster - Rasterize point layer (implemented; use webgl performance instead) raster.dpi - Rasterization DPI (applicable without .raster) show.grid.lines - Toggle grid lines (managed via Axes tab gridline controls) legend.color.breaks.labels - Labels color-scale breaks (implemented) new Lines tab provides enhanced functionality including multiple lines per type, individual line widths, opacities, diagonal/ablines slope control.

title: Input UI components for the scatterPlot module — dittoViz_scatterPlotInputsUI
text: following dittoViz::scatterPlot() parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: x.- X-axis variable (UI: "X Data", default: 2nd column) y.- Y-axis variable (UI: "Y Data", default: 3rd column) color.- Coloring variable (UI: "Color ", default: "") shape.- Shape variable (UI: "Shape ", default: "") split.- Faceting variable (UI: "Split ", default: "") rows.use - Row filter expression (UI: "Rows Filter", default: "") x.adjustment - X-axis adjustment (UI: "X Adjustment", default: "") y.adjustment - Y-axis adjustment (UI: "Y Adjustment", default: "") color.adjustment - Color adjustment (UI: "Color Adjustment", default: "") x.adj.fxn - X adjustment function (UI: "X Adjustment Function", default: "") y.adj.fxn - Y adjustment function (UI: "Y Adjustment Function", default: "") color.adj.fxn - Color adjustment function (UI: "Color Adjustment Function", default: "") size - Point size (UI: "Point Size", default: 1) size.- Numeric column mapped point size (UI: "Size ", default: ""); set, custom circle size legend drawn since plotly render native size legend opacity - Point opacity (UI: "Point Opacity", default: 1) show.others - Show others (UI: "Show Others", default: TRUE) split.show..others - Show split others (UI: "Show Split Others", default: TRUE) plot.order - Plot order (UI: "Plot Order", default: "unordered") shape.panel - Shape panel values (UI: "Shape Panel", default: "16, 15, 17, 23, 25, 8") min.color - Minimum color (UI: "Min Color", default: "#F0E442") max.color - Maximum color (UI: "Max Color", default: "#0072B2") contour.color - Contour color (UI: "Contour Color", default: "black") contour.linetype - Contour linetype (UI: "Contour Linetype", default: "solid") color.panel - Named character vector mapping color.levels colors, e.g. c(setosa = "#FF0000", virginica = "blue") (UI: color.panel.ui). Seeds picker; unnamed groups fall back default palette user edits take precedence. single.point.color - Point color used color.unset (UI: "Point color", default: "#000000") split.nrow - Number split rows (UI: "Rows", default: NA) split.ncol - Number split columns (UI: "Columns", default: NA) multivar.split.dir - Multivar split direction (UI: "Multivar Split Dir", default: "col") split.adjust.scales - Facet scales (UI: "Facet Scales", default: "fixed") annotate.- Annotate column (UI: "Annotate ", default: "") highlight.points - Points highlight (UI: "Points Highlight", default: "") highlight.color - Highlight fill (UI: "Highlight Fill", default: "#00FFF7") highlight.size - Highlight size (UI: "Highlight Size", default: 7) highlight.border.color - Highlight border color (UI: "Highlight Border Color", default: "#000000") highlight.border.width - Highlight border width (UI: "Highlight Border Width", default: 1) highlight.auto.annotate - Auto-annotate highlights (UI: "Auto-annotate Highlights", default: TRUE) annotation.color - Annotation color (UI: "Annotation Color", default: "black") annotation.ax - Annotation X offset (UI: "Annotation X Offset", default: 20) annotation.ay - Annotation Y offset (UI: "Annotation Y Offset", default: -20) annotation.size - Annotation size (UI: "Annotation Size", default: 10) annotation.showarrow - Show arrow (UI: "Show Arrow", default: TRUE) annotation.arrowcolor - Arrow color (UI: "Arrow Color", default: "black") annotation.arrowhead - Arrowhead style (UI: "Arrowhead Style", default: 2) annotation.arrowwidth - Arrow linewidth (UI: "Arrow Linewidth", default: 1.5) legend.color.breaks - Legend tick breaks (UI: "Legend Tick Breaks", default: "") size.legend.x - Custom size-legend x position (UI: "Size Legend X Position", default: 1.02); nudges manual size legend (drawn size.set) along x-axis. size.legend.y - Custom size-legend y position (UI: "Size Legend Y Position", default: 0.95); nudges manual size legend (drawn size.set) along y-axis. min.value - Minimum value (UI: "Min Value", default: NA) max.value - Maximum value (UI: "Max Value", default: NA) trajectory.group.- Trajectory group (UI: "Trajectory Group ", default: "") add.trajectory..groups - Add trajectory groups (UI: "Add Trajectory Groups", default: "") trajectory.arrow.size - Trajectory arrow size (UI: "Trajectory Arrow Size", default: 0.15) .ellipse - Enable ellipses (UI: "Enable Ellipses", default: FALSE) .contour - Enable contour (UI: "Enable Contour", default: FALSE) hover.data - Hover data columns (UI: "Hover Data", default: "") hover.round.digits - Hover round digits (UI: "Hover Round Digits", default: 5)

text: user inputs module separated outputs allow flexible UI design. inputs automatically organized grid layout via organize_inputs() function, columns controlling number columns grid. Defaults can set input providing named list values defaults argument. Nearly parameters dittoViz::yPlot() can set via inputs, see help function exhaustive list. "Y Data" input accepts several columns . "Multivar Aesthetic" (Facet tab) decides shown: "split" gives variable facet (alongside split.facets), "group" "color" put variables x-axis fill legend respectively. several variables Stats tab available "split" aesthetic split.set, comparisons run separately within variable's facet. layouts either replace x-axis groups compared facet two dimensions , neither significance brackets can placed .

what: Plot parameters not implemented or with altered functionality
title: Input UI components for the yPlot module — dittoViz_yPlotInputsUI
text: following dittoViz::yPlot() parameters available via UI inputs: xlab - X-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) ylab - Y-axis label (auto-generated reflect applied Y adjustment, e.g. "log2(z-score(units))"; plotly allows interactive editing). several Y variables adjustment shown, variables named facet strips legend instead main - Plot title (plotly allows interactive editing) sub - Plot subtitle (supported plotly) theme - ggplot2 theme (applicable plotly) legend.title - Legend title (managed plotly interactively) add.line - Use hline.intercepts instead horizontal lines full styling options line.linetype - Use hline.linetypes instead line.color - Use hline.colors instead line.linewidth - Use hline.widths instead line.opacity - Use hline.opacities instead rows.use - Row subset plot (implemented) colors - Integer index/order color.panel (managed via palette UI) shape.panel - Shapes used shape.(implemented) y.breaks - Custom continuous-axis breaks (implemented) x.labels - Override group labels (implemented) x.labels.rotate - Rotate group labels (handled Axes tab tick-angle controls) x.reorder - Reorder x-axis groups (implemented) boxplot.width - Boxplot width (controlled via boxgap boxgroupgap) boxplot.outlier.size - Outlier point size (implemented) boxplot.position.dodge - Boxplot dodge (controlled via boxgap) vlnplot.quantiles - Violin quantiles (translate plotly)

title: Input UI components for the yPlot module — dittoViz_yPlotInputsUI
text: following dittoViz::yPlot() parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: var - Y-axis variable(s) (UI: "Y Data", default: 2nd numeric variable). Several may selected; multivar.aes controls displayed multivar.aes - Aesthetic used multiple var columns (UI: "Multivar Aesthetic", default: "split") multivar.split.dir - Facet direction multiple var columns (UI: "Multivar Split Dir", default: "col") group.- Grouping variable x-axis (UI: "Group ", default: 2nd categorical variable) color.- Coloring variable (UI: "Color ", default: "") shape.- Shape variable (UI: "Shape ", default: "") split.- Faceting variable (UI: "Split (facet)", default: "") plots - Plot types show (UI: "Plots show", default: c("boxplot", "jitter")) color.panel - Custom color values (UI: palette picker, derived palette) min - Y-axis minimum (UI: "Y Axis Min", auto-calculated) max - Y-axis maximum (UI: "Y Axis Max", auto-calculated) var.adjustment - Y-axis data adjustment (UI: "Y Adjustment", default: "") var.adj.fxn - Y-axis adjustment function (UI: "Y Adjustment Function", default: "") split.nrow - Number facet rows (UI: "Rows", default: 4) split.ncol - Number facet columns (UI: "Columns", default: 4) split.adjust - Facet scale behavior (UI: "Facet Scaling", default: "fixed") .raster - Rasterize jitter points (UI: "Rasterize Jitter", default: FALSE) raster.dpi - DPI rasterization (UI: "Raster DPI", default: 600) jitter.size - Jitter point size (UI: "Jitter Point Size", default: 1) jitter.width - Jitter width (UI: "Jitter Width", default: 0.2) jitter.color - Jitter border color (UI: "Jitter Border Color", default: "#000000") jitter.shape.legend.size - Shape legend size (UI: "Shape Legend Size", default: 5) jitter.shape.legend.show - Show shape legend (UI: "Show Shape Legend", default: TRUE) jitter.position.dodge - Jitter position dodge (calculated boxgap) boxplot.show.outliers - Show boxplot outliers boxplot.color - Boxplot outline color (UI: "Boxplot Color", default: "#000000") boxplot.fill - Fill boxplot (UI: "Fill Boxplot", default: TRUE) boxplot.lineweight - Boxplot line weight (UI: "Boxplot Line Weight", default: 0.5) vlnplot.lineweight - Violin line weight (UI: "Violin Line Weight", default: 0.5) vlnplot.scaling - Violin scaling method (UI: "Violin Scaling", default: "area") vlnplot.width - Violin width (derived boxgap; directly settable) ridgeplot.lineweight - Ridge line weight (UI: "Ridge Line Weight", default: 0.5) ridgeplot.scale - Ridge overlap scale (UI: "Ridge Scale (overlap)", default: 1.25) ridgeplot.ymax.expansion - Ridge Y-max expansion (UI: "Ridge Y-max Expansion", default: NA) ridgeplot.shape - Ridge shape (UI: "Ridge Shape", default: "smooth") ridgeplot.bins - Ridge bins (UI: "Ridge Bins", default: 30) ridgeplot.binwidth - Ridge binwidth (UI: "Ridge Binwidth", default: NULL) hover.data - Columns shown hover (UI: "Hover Data", default: ""; empty uses sensible default set columns) hover.round.digits - Hover value rounding (UI: "Hover Round Digits", default: 5) legend.show - Show legend (always TRUE; directly settable)

text: following parameters implementing new functionality controlling plotly-specific features also available: boxmode - Boxplot mode grouping (calculated: "group" "overlay" based color.) boxgap - Boxplot position dodge (UI: "Boxplot Position Dodge", default: 0.3) boxgroupgap - Boxplot group dodge (UI: "Boxplot Group Dodge", default: 0.2) title.font.size - Plot title font size (UI: "Title Size", default: 26) title.font.family - Font family title text (UI: "Title Font", default: "Arial") title.font.color - Axis title font family (UI: "Axis Title Font", default: "Arial") axis.showline - Show axis border lines (UI: "Show Axis Lines", default: TRUE) axis.mirror - Mirror axis lines opposite side (UI: "Mirror Axis Lines", default: TRUE) show.grid.x - Show X-axis major gridlines (UI: "Show X Major Gridlines", default: TRUE) show.grid.y - Show Y-axis major gridlines (UI: "Show Y Major Gridlines", default: TRUE) axis.linecolor - Color axis lines (UI: "Axis Line Color", default: "black") axis.linewidth - Width axis lines (UI: "Axis Line Width", default: 0.5) axis.tickfont.size - Size tick labels (UI: "Tick Label Size", default: 12) axis.tickfont.color - Color tick labels (UI: "Tick Label Color", default: "black") axis.tickfont.family - Position tick marks (UI: "Tick Position", default: "outside") axis.tickcolor - Color tick marks (UI: "Tick Mark Color", default: "black") axis.ticklen - Length tick marks (UI: "Tick Mark Length", default: 5) axis.tickwidth - Width tick marks (UI: "Tick Mark Width", default: 1) hline.intercepts - Y-coordinates horizontal reference lines (UI: "Y-intercepts", default: "") hline.colors - Colors horizontal lines (UI: "Colors", default: "#000000") hline.widths - Widths horizontal lines (UI: "Widths", default: "1") hline.linetypes - Line types horizontal lines (UI: "Line Types", default: "dashed") hline.opacities - Opacities horizontal lines (UI: "Opacities (0-1)", default: "1") vline.intercepts - X-coordinates vertical reference lines (UI: "X-intercepts", default: "") vline.colors - Colors vertical lines (UI: "Colors", default: "#000000") vline.widths - Widths vertical lines (UI: "Widths", default: "1") vline.linetypes - Line types vertical lines (UI: "Line Types", default: "dashed") vline.opacities - Opacities vertical lines (UI: "Opacities (0-1)", default: "1") abline.slopes - Slopes diagonal reference lines (UI: "Slopes", default: "") abline.intercepts - Y-intercepts diagonal lines (UI: "Y-intercepts", default: "") abline.colors - Colors diagonal lines (UI: "Colors", default: "#000000") abline.widths - Widths diagonal lines (UI: "Widths", default: "1") abline.linetypes - Line types diagonal lines (UI: "Line Types", default: "dashed") abline.opacities - Opacities diagonal lines (UI: "Opacities (0-1)", default: "1") palette.colours - Named character vector mapping group levels colors, e.g. c(= "#FF0000", B = "blue") (UI: "Plot colors"). Seeds picker; unnamed groups fall back default palette user edits take precedence. annotate.- Column whose values identify label jitter points (UI: "Annotate ", default: "") highlight.points - Values annotate.column highlight (UI: "Points Highlight", default: "") highlight.color - Fill color highlighted points (UI: "Highlight Fill", default: "#00FFF7") highlight.size - Size highlighted points (UI: "Highlight Size", default: 7) highlight.border.color - Border color highlighted points (UI: "Highlight Border Color", default: "#000000") highlight.border.width - Border width highlighted points (UI: "Highlight Border Width", default: 1) highlight.auto.annotate - Label highlighted points automatically (UI: "Auto-annotate Highlights", default: TRUE) annotation.color - Annotation text color (UI: "Annotation Color", default: "black") annotation.ax - Horizontal label offset pixels (UI: "Annotation X Offset", default: 20) annotation.ay - Vertical label offset pixels (UI: "Annotation Y Offset", default: -20) annotation.size - Annotation font size (UI: "Annotation Size", default: 10) annotation.showarrow - Draw arrow label point (UI: "Show Arrow", default: TRUE) annotation.arrowcolor - Annotation arrow color (UI: "Arrow Color", default: "black") annotation.arrowhead - Annotation arrowhead style (UI: "Arrowhead Style", default: 2) annotation.arrowwidth - Annotation arrow line width (UI: "Arrow Linewidth", default: 1.5)

what: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot
title: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot
text: Generates customizable interactive dumbbell plot using plotly. Supports single dot mode (1 x variable) dumbbell mode (2 x variables), flexible coloring either X Y variables, faceting, transformations.

title: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot
code: dumbbellPlot(   data,   x,   y,   colour.by = "X variables",   palette.selection,   show.legend = TRUE,   facet.by = NULL,   line.colour = "gray80",   facet.scales = "fixed",   subplot.margin = 0.05,   axis.showline = TRUE,   axis.mirror = TRUE,   axis.linecolor = "black",   axis.linewidth = 0.5,   axis.tickfont.size = 12,   axis.tickfont.color = "black",   axis.tickfont.family = "Arial",   axis.tickangle.x = 0,   axis.tickangle.y = 0,   axis.ticks = "outside",   axis.tickcolor = "black",   axis.ticklen = 5,   axis.tickwidth = 1,   title.text = "",   title.font.size = 26,   title.font.family = "Arial",   title.font.color = "black",   title.x.position = 0.47,   y.title = NULL,   x.title = NULL,   flip.x = FALSE,   flip.y = FALSE,   x.adjustment = NULL,   order.by = NULL )

title: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot
text: data data.frame tibble containing data plot. x Character vector column name(s) x-axis values. Maximum 2 values allowed. 1 value: creates single dot plot. 2 values: creates dumbbell plot connecting segments. y Character, column name y-axis (categorical variable recommended). colour.Character, color markers. Options: "X variables" (different colors x variable) "Y variables" (different colors y category). Default: "X variables". palette.selection Character vector hex colors marker colors. show.legend Logical, whether display legend. Default: TRUE. facet.Optional character, column name facet plots . Creates subplots unique value. Default: NULL. line.colour Character, hex color connecting lines dumbbell points. Default: "gray80". facet.scales Character, controls axis scaling across facets. Options: "fixed" (), "free" (independent), "free_x" (independent x-axis), "free_y" (independent y-axis). Default: "fixed". subplot.margin Numeric, spacing facet panels fraction plot area. May single value (applied directions) length-2 vector c(horizontal, vertical) control gap columns rows separately. Default: 0.06. axis.showline Logical, whether show axis border lines. Default: TRUE. axis.mirror Logical, whether mirror axis lines opposite side plot. Default: TRUE. axis.linecolor Character, hex color axis lines. Default: "black". axis.linewidth Numeric, width axis lines pixels. Default: 0.5. axis.tickfont.size Numeric, font size axis tick labels. Default: 12. axis.tickfont.color Character, hex color axis tick labels. Default: "black". axis.tickfont.family Character, font family axis tick labels. Default: "Arial". axis.tickangle.x Numeric, rotation angle x-axis tick labels degrees. Default: 0. axis.tickangle.y Numeric, rotation angle y-axis tick labels degrees. Default: 0. axis.ticks Character, position tick marks. Options: "outside", "inside", "none". Default: "outside". axis.tickcolor Character, hex color tick marks. Default: "black". axis.ticklen Numeric, length tick marks pixels. Default: 5. axis.tickwidth Numeric, width tick marks pixels. Default: 1. title.text Character, main title text plot. Default: "". title.font.size Numeric, font size plot title. Default: 26. title.font.family Character, font family plot title. Default: "Arial". title.font.color Character, hex color plot title text. Default: "black". title.x.position Numeric, horizontal position plot title paper coordinates (0 = left, 1 = right). Default: 0.47. y.title Optional character, label y-axis. NULL, auto-generated column name. Default: NULL. x.title Optional character, label x-axis. NULL, auto-generated column name. Default: NULL. flip.x Logical, whether reverse x-axis direction. Default: FALSE. flip.y Logical, whether reverse y-axis direction. Default: FALSE. x.adjustment Optional character function, transformation apply x values. Options: "log2", "log", "log10", "neg_log10", "log1p", ".factor", "abs", "sqrt", custom function. Default: NULL. order.Optional character vector, column name(s) order data plotting. Default: NULL.

title: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot

title: Create an Interactive Dumbbell Plot with plotly — dumbbellPlot
text: dumbbell plot designed comparing two values across categories. Modes: Single dot mode (1 x variable): Shows one marker per y category Dumbbell mode (2 x variables): Shows two markers connected line per y category Coloring options: X variables: x variable gets different color (e.g., Male=blue, Female=pink) Y variables: y category gets different color (e.g., School =red, School B=blue)

text: Build multi-panel Figure Builder Shiny application returnable object. app lets users add VizModules plot module free-form A4 canvas, drag resize plot, filter plot's data independently, label panels automatically, export whole figure single editable SVG (bundle every plot's source data, HTML plot, statistics one .zip).

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
code: figureBuilderApp(   data_list = NULL,   module_registry = NULL,   title = "VizModules Figure Builder",   return_components = FALSE )

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
text: data_list optional named list data frames seed dataset registry. NULL (default), bundled example datasets (plus sales_by_product summary suited pie plot) used. least one element required every element must data frame. module_registry optional named list describing plot modules offer. NULL (default), bundled VizModules modules offered. entry list components: label (character, shown picker), dataset (character, dataset name defaults written ), inputs_ui, output_ui, server_fn (module's three functions), defaults (named list input defaults applied dataset chosen dataset). title character string used page title header (default: "VizModules Figure Builder"). return_components Logical. FALSE (default) shiny::shinyApp() object returned. TRUE named list ui server elements returned instead, convenient deployment scripts need explicit shinyApp(ui, server) call.

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
text: Either shiny::shinyApp() object, (return_components = TRUE) list elements ui server.

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
text: Datasets supplied via data_list seed "Add Plot" dialog; users can also upload additional datasets (CSV, TSV, TXT, RDS) runtime. set available plot modules controlled module_registry, app can extended custom wrapper modules without editing package. recommended way launch standalone Figure Builder. Internally thin wrapper around figureBuilderUI() / figureBuilderServer() Shiny module, builder can embedded inside larger app (instantiated ) calling two functions directly. bundled app system.file("apps/figure-builder", package = "VizModules") thin wrapper around function.

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
text: Jared Andrews

title: Create a VizModules Figure Builder Application — figureBuilderApp
code: library(VizModules)  # Launch with the bundled example datasets and all modules: app <- figureBuilderApp() if (interactive()) runApp(app)  # Launch with your own datasets: app2 <- figureBuilderApp(data_list = list("iris" = iris, "mtcars" = mtcars)) if (interactive()) runApp(app2)  # Return the UI and server separately (e.g. for a deployment app.R): parts <- figureBuilderApp(return_components = TRUE) if (interactive()) shinyApp(parts$ui, parts$server)

text: data data.frame tibble containing data plot. x Character vector column name(s) x-axis. Multiple columns create separate traces. y Character vector column name(s) y-axis. Multiple columns create separate traces. palette.selection Character vector hex colors line colors. Used assign colors groups traces. plot.mode Character, plotly mode plot type. Options: "lines", "markers", "lines+markers". Default: "lines". line.type Character, line style. Options: "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot". Default: NULL. show.legend Logical, whether display legend. Default: TRUE. facet.Optional character, column name facet plots . Creates subplots unique value. Default: NULL. facet.scales Character, controls axis scaling across facets. Options: "fixed" (), "free" (independent), "free_x" (independent x-axis), "free_y" (independent y-axis). Default: "fixed". facet.nrow Optional integer, number rows faceted subplot grid. NULL (default), single row used unless facet.ncol supplied, case number rows derived number facet levels. facet.ncol Optional integer, number columns faceted subplot grid. NULL (default), columns derived facet.nrow number facet levels. one facet.nrow / facet.ncol needs set; provided, facet.nrow takes precedence. subplot.margin Numeric, spacing facet panels fraction plot area. May single value (applied directions) length-2 vector c(horizontal, vertical) control gap columns rows separately. Default: 0.05. axis.showline Logical, whether show axis border lines. Default: TRUE. axis.mirror Logical, whether mirror axis lines opposite side plot. Default: TRUE. axis.linecolor Character, hex color axis lines. Default: "black". axis.linewidth Numeric, width axis lines pixels. Default: 0.5. axis.tickfont.size Numeric, font size axis tick labels. Default: 12. axis.tickfont.color Character, hex color axis tick labels. Default: "black". axis.tickfont.family Character, font family axis tick labels. Default: "Arial". axis.tickangle.x Numeric, rotation angle x-axis tick labels degrees. Default: 0. axis.tickangle.y Numeric, rotation angle y-axis tick labels degrees. Default: 0. axis.ticks Character, position tick marks. Options: "outside", "inside", "none". Default: "outside". axis.tickcolor Character, hex color tick marks. Default: "black". axis.ticklen Numeric, length tick marks pixels. Default: 5. axis.tickwidth Numeric, width tick marks pixels. Default: 1. show.grid.x Logical, whether show gridlines x-axis. Default: TRUE. show.grid.y Logical, whether show gridlines y-axis. Default: TRUE. title.text Character, main title text plot. Default: "". title.font.size Numeric, font size plot title. Default: 14. title.font.family Character, font family plot title. Default: "Arial". title.font.color Character, hex color plot title text. Default: "black". title.x.position Numeric, horizontal position plot title paper coordinates (0 = left, 1 = right). Default: 0.47. y.title Optional character, label y-axis. NULL, auto-generated column name. x single categorical column, plotted y-values per-group means, title wrapped mean(<y.title>) accurately describe summary displayed. Default: NULL. x.title Optional character, label x-axis. NULL, auto-generated column name. Default: NULL. flip.x Logical, whether reverse x-axis direction. Default: FALSE. flip.y Logical, whether reverse y-axis direction. Default: FALSE. x.adjustment Optional character function, transformation apply x values. Options: "log2", "log", "log10", "neg_log10", "log1p", ".factor", "abs", "sqrt", custom function. Default: NULL. y.adjustment Optional character function, transformation apply y values. Options: "log2", "log", "log10", "neg_log10", "log1p", ".factor", "abs", "sqrt", custom function. Default: NULL. color.adjustment Optional character function, transformation apply color grouping variable. options x.adjustment y.adjustment. Default: NULL. order.Optional character vector, column name(s) order data plotting. Default: NULL. error.colour hex colour input set colour error bars plot categorical X axis 1 Y axis variable error.width numeric input set width error bars plot categorical X axis 1 Y axis variable error.bar Boolean value determine error bars plot categorical X axis 1 Y axis variable

what: Plot parameters not implemented or with altered functionality
title: Input UI components for the DotPlot module — plotthis_DotPlotInputsUI
text: following plotthis::DotPlot() parameters available via UI inputs: xlab - X-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) ylab - Y-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) title - Plot title (plotly allows interactive editing) subtitle - Plot subtitle (supported plotly) aspect.ratio - Aspect ratio control (handled plotly layout) legend.position - Legend positioning (plotly allows interactive repositioning) legend.direction - Legend orientation (plotly allows interactive adjustment) x_sep - Separator multiple x columns (yet implemented) y_sep - Separator multiple y columns (yet implemented) split_by - Split variable separate plots (work plotly; facet_by available instead) split_by_sep - Separator multiple split_by columns (split_by used module) size_name - Size legend name (plotly allows interactive editing) fill_name - Fill legend name (yet implemented) fill_cutoff_name - Fill cutoff legend name (yet implemented) theme - ggplot2 theme (managed internally) theme_args - Theme arguments (yet implemented) palcolor - Managed internally via palette selection UI border_alpha - Dot border transparency (exposed; uses plotthis default 1) add_bg - Add background stripes/shading (yet implemented) bg_palette - Background palette (yet implemented) bg_palcolor - Background palette colors (yet implemented) bg_alpha - Background alpha (yet implemented) bg_direction - Background stripe direction (yet implemented) x_text_angle - X-axis text angle (handled axis.tickangle.x) keep_empty - Keep empty factor levels (yet implemented) keep_na - Keep NA values (yet implemented) combine - Combine multiple plots (applicable split_by implemented) seed - Random seed (applicable) nrow - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) ncol - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) byrow - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) axes - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) axis_titles - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) guides - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module) design - applies split_by used combine (split_by used module)

title: Input UI components for the DotPlot module — plotthis_DotPlotInputsUI
text: following plotthis::DotPlot() custom parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: x - X-axis variable (UI: "X Values", default: 2nd categorical variable) y - Y-axis variable (UI: "Y Values", default: 3rd categorical variable) size_by - Numeric column mapped dot size (UI: "Size ", default: "" = count) size_min - Minimum dot size (UI: "Min Dot Size", default: 1) size_max - Maximum dot size (UI: "Max Dot Size", default: 6) fill_by - Numeric column mapped dot fill (UI: "Fill ", default: "") fill_cutoff - Cutoff applied fill column (UI: "Fill Cutoff", default: NA) fill_cutoff_direction - Direction fill cutoff (UI: "Fill Cutoff Direction", default: "<"); combined fill_cutoff plotthis expression "< 18". flip - Flip x y axes (UI: "Rotate (swap X/Y)", default: FALSE) facet_by - Faceting variable (UI: "Facet ", default: "") facet_scales - Facet scale behavior (UI: "Facet Scale", default: "fixed") facet_ncol - Number facet columns (UI: "Columns", default: NULL) facet_nrow - Number facet rows (UI: "Rows", default: NULL) facet_byrow - Facet ordering direction (UI: "Facet Row", default: TRUE) palette.name - Continuous fill palette (UI: "Color Palette", default: "Spectral") palreverse - Reverse color palette (UI: "Reverse palette", default: FALSE) alpha - Dot fill transparency (UI: "Alpha", default: 1) border_color - Dot border color; constant colors supported (UI: "Border Color", default: "black") border_size - Dot border stroke width (UI: "Border Size", default: 0.5) lower_quantile - Lower quantile continuous fill color scale (UI: "Lower Quantile", default: 0) upper_quantile - Upper quantile continuous fill color scale (UI: "Upper Quantile", default: 1) lower_cutoff - Explicit lower cutoff continuous fill color scale (UI: "Lower Cutoff", default: NA); overrides lower_quantile set upper_cutoff - Explicit upper cutoff continuous fill color scale (UI: "Upper Cutoff", default: NA); overrides upper_quantile set size.legend.x - Custom size-legend x position (UI: "Size Legend X Position", default: 1.04); nudges manual size legend (drawn size.set) along x-axis. size.legend.y - Custom size-legend y position (UI: "Size Legend Y Position", default: 0.35); nudges manual size legend (drawn size.set) along y-axis.

text: following plotthis::Histogram() parameters available via UI inputs: xlab - X-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) ylab - Y-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) title - Plot title (plotly allows interactive editing) subtitle - Plot subtitle (supported plotly) legend.position - Legend positioning (plotly allows interactive repositioning) group_by_sep - Separator group columns (applicable UI context) group_name - Group legend name (handled plotly) xtrans - X-axis transformation (implemented UI) ytrans - Y-axis transformation (implemented UI) split_by - Split variable (returns patchwork object, supported plotly), use facet_by instead split_by_sep - applies split_by used theme - ggplot2 theme (applicable plotly) theme_args - Theme arguments (applicable plotly) palette - Managed internally via palette selection UI expand - Axis expansion (implemented) seed - Random seed (applicable) combine - applies split_by used nrow - applies split_by used ncol - applies split_by used byrow - applies split_by used axes - applies split_by used axis_titles - applies split_by used guides - applies split_by used design - applies split_by used palreverse - Reverse color palette (implemented) aspect.ratio - Aspect ratio control (handled plotly layout) keep_empty - Keep empty factor levels (implemented) keep_na - Keep NA values (implemented) legend.direction - Managed position legend however can handled via plotly

title: Input UI components for the ViolinPlot module — plotthis_ViolinPlotInputsUI
text: following plotthis::ViolinPlot() parameters available via UI inputs: xlab - X-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) ylab - Y-axis label (plotly allows interactive editing) title - Plot title (plotly allows interactive editing) subtitle - Plot subtitle (supported plotly) aspect.ratio - Aspect ratio control (handled plotly layout) legend.position - Legend positioning (plotly allows interactive repositioning) x_sep - Separator x columns (applicable UI context) in_form - Data input format (applicable - always long form) split_by - Split variable (returns patchwork object, supported plotly), use facet_by instead split_by_sep - applies split_by used symnum_args - Significance symbol arguments (Stats tab manages symbol display) keep_empty - Keep empty values (implemented) keep_na - Keep NA values (implemented) group_by_sep - Separator group columns (applicable UI context) group_name - Group legend name (handled plotly) paired_by - Pairing variable paired tests (use Stats tab "Paired Test" input instead) x_text_angle - X-axis text angle (handled plotly axis settings) step_increase - Step increase significance brackets (set via Stats tab "Bracket Spacing") fill_mode - Fill mode grouped data (handled automatically) position_dodge_preserve - Preserve dodge width (implemented) theme - ggplot2 theme (applicable plotly) theme_args - Theme arguments (applicable plotly) palette - Managed internally via palette selection UI palreverse - Reverse color palette (implemented) alpha - Alpha transparency (implemented UI) stack - Stack violins (implemented) add_beeswarm - Add beeswarm points (implemented UI) beeswarm_method - Beeswarm arrangement method (implemented) beeswarm_cex - Beeswarm point size factor (implemented) beeswarm_priority - Beeswarm priority order (implemented) beeswarm_dodge - Beeswarm dodge width (implemented) add_trend - Add trend line (implemented UI) trend_color - Trend line color (implemented) trend_linewidth - Trend line width (implemented) trend_ptsize - Trend point size (implemented) add_stat - Add statistical annotation (implemented) stat_name - Statistical test name (implemented) stat_color - Statistical annotation color (implemented) stat_size - Statistical annotation size (implemented) stat_stroke - Statistical annotation stroke (implemented) stat_shape - Statistical annotation shape (implemented) add_bg - Add background shading (implemented) bg_palette - Background palette (implemented) bg_palcolor - Background color (implemented) bg_alpha - Background transparency (implemented) add_line - Add horizontal line (implemented UI - use Lines tab) line_color - Line color (implemented) line_width - Line width (implemented) line_type - Line type (implemented) comparisons - plotthis pairwise comparisons passed; equivalent pairwise significance testing provided via module's Stats tab (see "Statistical annotation parameters") ref_group - Reference group comparisons (use Stats tab instead) pairwise_method - Pairwise test method (set via Stats tab "Test" input instead) multiplegroup_comparisons - Multiple-group comparison flag (use Stats tab instead) multiple_method - Multiple-group test method (set via Stats tab "Test" input instead) sig_label - Significance label format (set via Stats tab "Display" input instead) sig_labelsize - Significance label size (handled Stats tab) hide_ns - Hide non-significant comparisons (use Stats tab "Hide Non-Significant" input) seed - Random seed (applicable) combine - applies split_by used nrow - applies split_by used ncol - applies split_by used byrow - applies split_by used axes - applies split_by used axis_titles - applies split_by used guides - applies split_by used legend.direction - Managed position legend however can handled via plotly

title: Input UI components for the ViolinPlot module — plotthis_ViolinPlotInputsUI
text: following plotthis::ViolinPlot() parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: x - X-axis variable (UI: "X Data", default: 2nd categorical variable) y - Y-axis variable (UI: "Y Data", default: 2nd numeric variable) group_by - Grouping variable (UI: "Group ", default: "") flip - Flip/swap x y axes (UI: "Rotate (swap X/Y)", default: FALSE) sort_x - Sort X-axis statistic (UI: "Sort X ", default: "none") y_max - Maximum Y-axis value (UI: "Y Max", default: calculated) y_min - Minimum Y-axis value (UI: "Y Min", default: calculated) add_point - Add jitter points (UI: "Add Jitter Points", default: FALSE) pt_size - Point size (UI: "Point Size", default: 1) pt_alpha - Point transparency (UI: "Point Alpha", default: 1) jitter_width - Jitter width (UI: "Jitter Width", default: 0.5) jitter_height - Jitter height (UI: "Jitter Height", default: 0) pt_color - Point outline color (UI: "Point Outline Colour", default: "#000000") add_box - Add box plot overlay (UI: "Add Box", default: FALSE) box_color - Box outline color (UI: "Box Colour", default: "#000000") box_width - Box width (UI: "Box Width", default: 0.1) box_ptsize - Box point size (UI: "Box Point Size", default: 2.5) highlight - Highlight condition (UI: "Highlight", default: "") highlight_color - Highlight color (UI: "Highlight Colour", default: "#000000") highlight_size - Highlight size (UI: "Highlight Size", default: 1) highlight_alpha - Highlight transparency (UI: "Highlight Alpha", default: 1) facet_by - Faceting variable (UI: "Facet ", default: "") facet_scales - Facet scale behavior (UI: "Facet Scale", default: "fixed") facet_ncol - Number facet columns (UI: "Columns", default: NULL) facet_nrow - Number facet rows (UI: "Rows", default: NULL) facet_byrow - Facet ordering direction (UI: "Facet Row", default: TRUE) palcolor - Custom color values (UI: palette picker, derived palette)

title: Input UI components for the ViolinPlot module — plotthis_ViolinPlotInputsUI
text: module provides plotly-based significance testing via Stats tab. following inputs available: stats.enabled - Enable statistical annotations (UI: "Enable Stats", default: FALSE) stat.test - Test apply: Wilcoxon, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA (UI: "Test") stat.p.adjust - P-value adjustment method (UI: "P-value Adjustment", default: "holm") stat.display - Value display: adjusted p-value, p-value, symbols (UI: "Display") stat.sig.threshold - Significance threshold symbols/hiding (UI: "Significance Threshold") stat.hide.ns - Hide non-significant comparisons (UI: "Hide Non-Significant", default: FALSE) stat.paired - Use paired test (UI: "Paired Test", default: FALSE) stat.pairs - Group comparisons test (UI: "Comparisons", multiple selection) stat.line.color - Bracket line color (UI: "Line Color", default: "#000000") stat.line.width - Bracket line width (UI: "Line Width") stat.bracket.style - Bracket style, capped flat (UI: "Bracket Style") stat.step.increase - Vertical spacing stacked brackets (UI: "Bracket Spacing") stat.text.bump - Offset significance text bracket (UI: "Text Offset") stat.bracket.inset - Horizontal inset brackets (UI: "Bracket Inset") stat.per.facet - Compute statistics independently per facet panel (UI: "Per Facet Panel")

title: Create a plotly radar chart — radarPlot
text: df data frame containing data plot. single trace, provide columns categories (theta) values (r). multiple traces, include grouping column. function automatically closes radar polygon adding first point end. theta Character, name column use angular categories (axes). r Character, name column use radial values. group Optional character, name column use grouping multiple traces. NULL, single trace plotted. Default: NULL. colors Optional character vector hex colors traces. named, values matched group values; otherwise colours recycled. palette Optional character vector fallback colors used colors supplied missing values present. fill Logical character, whether fill area trace. Use "toself" fill first point, FALSE fill. Default: "toself". line.width Numeric, width trace lines pixels. Default: 2. line.dash Character, line dash style. Options: "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot". Default: "solid". marker.size Numeric, size markers trace. Default: 5. marker.symbol Character, marker symbol. Options: "circle", "square", "diamond", "cross", "x", "triangle-", etc. Default: "circle". opacity Numeric, opacity traces (0-1). Default: 0.6. radial.visible Logical, whether show radial axis. Default: TRUE. radial.range Optional numeric vector length 2 specifying range radial axis (e.g., c(0, 100)). NULL, automatically determined. Default: NULL. radial.showline Logical, whether show radial axis line. Default: TRUE. radial.linecolor Character, hex color radial axis line. Default: "#444444". radial.gridcolor Character, hex color radial grid lines. Default: "#EEEEEE". angular.direction Character, direction angular axis. Options: "clockwise" "counterclockwise". Default: "clockwise". angular.rotation Numeric, rotation angle angular axis degrees. Default: 90. angular.gridcolor Character, hex color angular grid lines. Default: "#EEEEEE". show.legend Logical, whether display legend. Default: TRUE. legend.orientation Character, legend orientation. Options: "h" (horizontal) "v" (vertical). Default: "h". legend.x Numeric, horizontal legend position offset (0-1). Default: 0.5. legend.y Numeric, vertical legend position offset (-1 1). Default: -0.1. legend.font.family Character, font family legend text. Default: "Arial". legend.font.size Numeric, font size legend text. Default: 12. legend.font.color Character, hex color legend text. Default: "#000000". title.text Character, main plot title text. Default: "". title.font.family Character, font family title text. Default: "Arial". title.font.size Numeric, font size title text. Default: 18. title.font.color Character, hex color title text. Default: "#000000". title.x Numeric, horizontal position plot title (0-1). Default: 0.5. bgcolor Character, hex color plot background. Default: "#FFFFFF". polar.bgcolor Character, hex color polar area background. Default: "#FFFFFF".

text: following radarPlot() parameters can accessed via UI inputs /defaults argument: theta - Category column angular axes (UI: "Category column (theta)", default: 1st categorical column) r - Values column radial distance (UI: "Values column (r)", default: 1st numeric column) group - Optional grouping column multiple traces (UI: "Group column", default: NULL) fill - Fill area trace (UI: "Fill area", default: "toself") line.width - Line width (UI: "Line width", default: 2) line.dash - Line dash style (UI: "Line style", default: "solid") marker.size - Marker size (UI: "Marker size", default: 5) marker.symbol - Marker symbol (UI: "Marker symbol", default: "circle") opacity - Trace opacity (UI: "Opacity", default: 0.6) colors - Trace colors (UI: color picker, derived palette) radial.visible - Show radial axis (UI: "Show radial axis", default: TRUE) radial.range - Radial axis range (UI: "Radial min" "Radial max", default: auto) radial.showline - Show radial axis line (UI: "Show radial line", default: TRUE) radial.linecolor - Radial axis line color (UI: "Radial line color", default: "#444444") radial.gridcolor - Radial grid color (UI: "Radial grid color", default: "#EEEEEE") angular.direction - Angular axis direction (UI: "Angular direction", default: "clockwise") angular.rotation - Angular axis rotation (UI: "Angular rotation", default: 90) angular.gridcolor - Angular grid color (UI: "Angular grid color", default: "#EEEEEE") title.x - Title horizontal position (UI: "Title horizontal position", default: 0.5) title.font.size - Plot title font size (UI: "Title Size", default: 26) title.font.family - Font family title text (UI: "Title Font", default: "Arial") title.font.color - Color plot title (UI: "Title Color", default: "#000000") show.legend - Show legend (UI: "Show legend", default: TRUE) legend.orientation - Legend orientation (UI: "Legend orientation", default: "h") legend.font.family - Legend font (UI: "Legend font", default: "Arial") legend.font.size - Legend font size (UI: "Legend font size", default: 12) legend.font.color - Legend font color (UI: "Legend font color", default: "#000000") bgcolor - Plot background color (UI: "Plot background color", default: "#FFFFFF") polar.bgcolor - Polar area background color (UI: "Polar area background", default: "#FFFFFF") trace.colors - Named character vector mapping group levels colors, e.g. c(= "#FF0000", B = "blue") (UI: "Trace colors"). Seeds picker; unnamed groups fall back default palette user edits take precedence. single.color - Trace color used grouping set (UI: "Trace color:", default: "#1F77B4")

code: # Install into a temporary project rather than the current one: use_vizmodules_skills(tempdir()) #> Installed 'vizmodules-app'. #> Installed 'vizmodules-custom-module'. #> Installed 'vizmodules-new-module'. #>  #> 3 skill(s) written to '/tmp/RtmpW9x3L3/.agents/skills'. #> Restart your agent session if it was already running, so the new directory is picked up.  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Install into the current project, refreshing any that already exist: use_vizmodules_skills(".", overwrite = TRUE)  # Install for Claude Code specifically: use_vizmodules_skills(".", client = "claude") } # }

what: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
text: Parses expression text walks AST ensure contains allowed operations (comparisons, logical operators, column references, literals). Returns original string valid, NULL input empty, unparseable, contains disallowed operations. useful expression string must passed downstream function (e.g., plotthis::BoxPlot(highlight = ...)) rather evaluated directly.

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
code: validate_expression(expr_text, col_names)

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
text: expr_text Character string containing expression validate (e.g., "group == '' & value > 10"). col_names Character vector allowed column/symbol names (typically names(data)).

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
text: original expr_text string safe, NULL.

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
text: Use module passes user-typed expression string external plotting function evaluate internally. string validated executed function.

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
text: Jared Andrews

title: Validate a user-provided expression string for safety — validate_expression
code: validate_expression("Sepal.Length > 5", names(iris)) #> [1] "Sepal.Length > 5" validate_expression("system('echo pwned')", names(iris)) # NULL + warning #> Warning: Expression contains disallowed operations. Only column references, comparisons, and logical operators are permitted. #> NULL validate_expression("", names(iris)) # NULL #> NULL

what: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
text: drop-replacement shiny::selectInput() built shinyWidgets::virtualSelectInput(). underlying virtual-select library renders visible slice choice list, column tens thousands unique values stays responsive readable instead producing unusable wall options.

title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
code: viz_select_input(   inputId,   label,   choices,   selected = NULL,   multiple = FALSE,   search = NULL,   width = "100%",   ... )

title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
text: inputId input slot used access value. label Display label control, NULL label. choices vector named list values select , form accepted shiny::selectInput(). selected initially selected value(s). Defaults first choice single selects nothing multiple selects. multiple Logical, whether multiple values can selected. search Logical, whether show search box. Defaults NULL, enables search box 10 choices. width width input, e.g. "100%" "400px". ... arguments passed shinyWidgets::virtualSelectInput(), including raw virtual-select property optionsCount zIndex.

title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
text: shiny.tag object included UI definition.

title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input
text: Defaults chosen behaves like shiny::selectInput(): selected supplied multiple = FALSE, first choice selected. empty-string choice ("selection" convention used throughout package) relabelled "(none)" visible dropdown, value remains "".

title: Create a select input that scales to very large choice sets — viz_select_input

title: VizModules 0.4.0
text: Comes new example_composition demo dataset containing 1800 simulated single-cell records twelve donors nested inside two conditions (crossed two batches). Row annotations come extra columns input data frame; column annotations need companion per-sample metadata table, supplied via data = list(matrix = <data.frame>, column_annotations = <data.frame>) instead plain data frame. interactive output can split independently-placed pieces — ComplexHeatmap_HeatmapMainOutputUI(), ComplexHeatmap_HeatmapSubOutputUI(), ComplexHeatmap_HeatmapInfoOutputUI() — apps want main heatmap, sub-heatmap, click/brush info panel separate layout locations. title: VizModules 0.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-16 Created Figure Builder app users can dynamically construct multi-panel figures using different data sets plot types single page. Allows full page SVG export, source data dump organized per panel, full customization plot position size. *OutputUI() functions gained resizable argument (default TRUE). FALSE, plot output longer wrapped shinyjqui::jqui_resizable(), avoids redundant resize handle output embedded container already provides resizing (Figure Builder app cards). Added new plotthis_DotPlot module (plotthis_DotPlotInputsUI(), plotthis_DotPlotOutputUI(), plotthis_DotPlotServer(), plotthis_DotPlotApp() convenience wrapper) wraps plotthis::DotPlot() interactive dot plots, including custom dot-size legend since plotly still lacks capability. Added example_markers dataset, simulated single-cell marker-gene expression table (immune cell types × marker genes) used default example data DotPlot module. Added “Source Data” download button bottom every module’s control panel. button creates downloads ZIP file containing self-contained HTML plotly plot, CSV plot data (retrieved via plotly::plotly_data()), modules statistics enabled (Box / Violin / yPlot), table statistics info. Source downloads now built exported collect_source_data() create_source_download_handler() helpers, module server returns source reactive can reused (e.g. Figure Builder). Given source data now required many journals, important. Removed old interactive plot download button associated helper function. Removed old dynamically hidden stats download button associated logic, since stats now included source download applicable. Statistic helper functions now exported allowing users annotate plotly graphs custom statistics: compute_pairwise_stats(), create_stat_annotations(), apply_stat_annotations(), generate_pair_strings(), parse_pair_strings(). Exposed empty_plot() use placeholder, e.g. parameters aren’t valid given plot type, pass info user without ugly error messages. Faceting improvements - new internal helpers control subplot spacing, subplot size, facet_scale handling. fixes much wonkiness plots many panels. Uniform inputs added panel spacing across modules. Axis titles now uniformly added annotations allow interactive repositioning. Condensed package wide workflows simple helpers, e.g. apply_title_layout(), resulting significantly less jank. Axis adjustments now properly reflected axis/legend titles appropriate modules, e.g. yPlot, scatterPlot, linePlot. Removed handful spurious/non-functional inputs, particularly dittoViz_scatterPlot module. Custom size.legends added plotthis_DotPlot dittoViz_scatterPlot modules, since plotly yet support . Update docstrings reflect new inputs features clarify parameters underlying plotting functions may implemented. Various border fixes faceted plots.
